title: Uniform Validity of Multiplier Inference for Selector-Specific Transport Bounds with Rare Margins
banked_reason: Final math referee PASS established a sound incremental record, but delivered tier=incremental is below floor=field and paper_score_ceiling 4.3 < 7.4; the original cycle/flow-certificate kernel remains unfulfilled.
gap_reasons: The core delivers the standard finite transport image and selector-by-selector SCM attainment, but omits the proposal-headlined effective-support alternating-cycle point-identification iff and endpoint flow-certificate theorem; its own honest scope confirms this weaker kernel.

The flagship negative result targets a note-defined Hong--Li-style implementation rather than a specifically identified published estimator/workflow, and its sole witness has collapsing response variance with no nondegenerate observable-law or perturbation-stable generic-class certificate; this is a novelty revise with a subfield ceiling.

The exact selector interval is standard finite transportation geometry, while the SCM result only realizes that geometry inside the note's explicitly free, selector-specific abstraction class and does not preserve a common canonical Layer-3 map.
proof_attempt_summary: The run attempted a field-level sharp selector-envelope and changing-support inference package. The effective-support cycle criterion and endpoint flow-certificate kernel were retracted when they were not discharged; the repaired incremental record instead retains sound selector-specific SCM attainment, standard transport geometry, and a sharp but boundary-degenerate zero-coverage diagnostic with an honest projection fallback. A future retry would need a response-interior uniform coverage theorem plus either a genuine rare-margin converse or a concrete comparative rate/width advantage.
tldr: The selector-specific SCM construction yields an exact causal transport image, an incremental application of standard finite coupling geometry rather than a new transport identification theorem. The new uniform result is a diagnostic for the direct Hong--Li-style paired multiplier numerical-delta implementation defined here: on one fixed-margin, fixed-cell singleton with response means \(2b_n/n\), both absolute bounded-Lipschitz Gaussian approximations vanish while its envelope has coverage tending to zero for every deterministic step schedule. This does not refute Hong and Li's theorem and is not an impossibility result: the witness has collapsing response variance, lacks any fixed response-interiority or nondegenerate-variance bound, and projecting an honest simultaneous primitive region through \(L\) and \(U\) yields an honest fallback. Comparative width and shrinking-margin rates remain open on an explicitly response-interior subclass.
gap: Cho--Russell give uniformly valid but deliberately conservative inference from fixed nonvanishing random LP perturbations, while Gafarov gives uniformly valid sharp affine-set projection inference under uniform positive rank and slack constants and allows flat primal faces. Those results do not settle the validity or sharp boundary of the row-feasible paired numerical-delta procedure when transport margins and response cells shrink.
fill: The project defines \(\mathfrak P_{\kappa}^{0}\) independently of tuning, asks sufficiency under the only proposed rare-cell step window, and separately asks the for-every-schedule sharpness question. The two-branch \(2\times2\) handle distinguishes feasibility-correction distortion from optimal-face localization failure.
